steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 16 muffin cups or line with paper liners.

Stir flour, sugar, cornmeal, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Whisk milk, plantains, oil, eggs, and butter together in a separate bowl; stir in flour mixture until just combined. Do not overmix batter. Rest batter at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden and tops spring back when lightly pressed, 15 to 18 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Plantain Corn Muffins
raw_recipe.description: For this plaintain corn muffin recipe, ripe plantains and cornmeal along with sugar, milk, and melted butter help make the muffins simple and tasty.
raw_recipe.name: Plantain Corn Muffins

review.reviewBody: These are delicious! I modified it to be gluten-free using Bob's Red Mill all purpose GF flour and guar gum, but otherwise stuck to the recipe exactly. They are delicious as muffins, and I also tried just putting it in an 8x8 dish and baking it as cornbread - they still came out moist, sweet and flavorfull :) Yum!

You are a genius! All the ways I love plantains this will be another favorite! I changed a couple things only due to staying away from gluten in wheat and still turned out perfect. I used 1 and 1/2 cups of corn meal, left out the sugar. Ripe plantains are so sweet I did not think needed it.I loved that I could make these without the sugar. I made half the batch with some whole kernel corn. Also very good. The corn gives texture, yet sweetness and more of a savory note. These were so moist. I did have to bake for about 23 minutes.Thank you for sharing your great idea! This will be perfect for a spicy black bean soup to balance the heat!

These are great - store in the fridge for upto a week to maintain quality. Even if my plantains are super ripe I like to boil them in the skins before hand which ensures an easy mash. I cut the sugar and salt in half and added chili flakes and chopped fresh mint. Really great recipe - thanks so much for creating.

Instead of making muffins, I put it in an 8X8 pan. I also used buttermilk instead of milk. It took a little longer to bake, but so worth it! This was so good. The whole family enjoyed it. I also think adding some spice to it would be good too. Will make again.

I made three batches today. One batch for my toddlers using this recipe and adding an additional two tablespoons of ambrosia honey. The second batch was made for my husband and I just added diced candied jakepenos. The third batch I substituted milk with almond milk, and flour with almond flour, and added candied jalepenos! All three turned out great thanks for sharing!

Thanks for sharing such a creative recipe. I love plantains and corn muffins, genius idea. I made these without eggs and use 1/3 cup drained crushed pineapple & 2 cups mashed (almost black ripe) plantains. If you use soy milk and earth balance this would be a vegan muffin.

I tried this using a bunch of substitution, instead of the sugar i used splenda, i used olive oil instead of corn oil and used the silk milk instead of regular milk. Everyone enjoyed it and asked for seconds. It was awesome and healthy. Even the kids enjoyed it.

These were very tasty but a bit on the sweet side for my taste. I will cut back on the sugar next time. Thank you for adding yet another fantastic way to use plantains. In a Cuban/French/American household, you can imagine how many different ways we use them already.
Always tastes great. A favorite among my colleagues.

I just made this as a gluten free recipe using Arthur’s all purpose GF. I used olive oil to substitute the corn oil and skipped the butter. I am Caribbean so I added a little bit of Cinnamon and Ginger powder. A can of coconut milk since I doubled the recipe and because my plantains were frozen and very ripe I used 3 of them. Didn’t use a mixer but I softened the plantains with the food processor first and whisk all the ingredients in. I will never let my plantains go to waste again.
I doubled the ingredients it came out moist and tasty. Love it and love making muffins
turned out really good. excellent base for a fruit cup!
I made it gluten free by substituting my GF flour mix and it still taste great. Even the kids liked it. I great way to use up plantains!
Made this because my husband accidentally bought plantains. This ended up being a great recipe and we will for sure be making them again.
A very good recipe and quick/ easy.
These were PERFECT, a great recipe when you keep putting off using the last 1 or 2 plantains. They were light, flavorful and delicious, they definitely did not last long in our family of 4.
